about: Every change between SDK 2 and SDK 3, as data. kind: "renamed" = the same call under a new name (mechanical: true means a script may rename it: same arguments, same result unless a "list" entry for the new name says otherwise); "removed" = no like-for-like call, the note says what to do ("to" names the nearest replacement); "option" = an option or argument that went; "option" entries with "argument" name the position (0 = first) of an argument a script may drop when it is the last one passed; "list" = a function that now returns ListResult<T> = { items, nextCursor, count? } ("paged" says whether it takes limit + cursor); "behaviour" = something that changes at run time and the compiler cannot see.

hold.when: The app calls a writing function of the old `attestation` namespace (singular): attestation.create, attestation.update, attestation.remove.
hold.why: Its data has not been moved to the new `attestations` yet. SDK 3 keeps the namespace so the app still builds; leave those calls as they are.

unchanged: The old `attestation` namespace (deprecated, kept until its data is moved).
`ctx.sl.*` inside an app's server functions: it runs on the server and keeps its shapes.
The standard query functions (proof.query, contact.query, products.standardQuery, app.records.query).
Every function that is not a list and was not deprecated.

changes.note: The API never had this address, so the call could only fail. Find the orders that hold items with `order.query(collectionId, { query: { items: [{ itemType, itemId }] } })`.

changes.name: analytics.admin.events
changes.before: { source, limit, offset, sort, count, rows }
changes.note: `limit` and `cursor` go at the top level of the body. The old `count` was the rows on this page; it is gone. Sorting is now orderBy: [{ timestamp: 'asc' }] (or 'desc', the default); `sort: 'asc' | 'desc'` is gone. limit, cursor, from and to are unchanged. The answer still carries `sort: 'ASC' | 'DESC'`.

changes.name: app.cases.list
changes.before: { data, pagination: { total, limit, offset, hasMore } }
changes.note: `sort: 'priority:desc'` becomes `orderBy: [{ priority: 'desc' }]` (fields: createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt, priority, status, category, ref, customId, sourceSystem). `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `closedAt` keep their names but are now a range object `{ gte, lte }`; the old string form ('gte:2024-01-01' or a bare date) is gone. An option set to an empty string is now left out of the request instead of being sent empty.

changes.name: app.options.get
changes.before: { items, version, mode, total? } | { unchanged: true, version }
changes.note: `total` is `count`. The `{ unchanged: true, version }` answer is as before. A picker is now paged: it answers 50 entries unless you give `limit` (at most 1000), and `nextCursor` is no longer always null. An app that needs every entry must follow `nextCursor` or ask for a larger `limit`. `q`, `version` and `admin` are unchanged.

changes.name: app.records.list
changes.before: { data, pagination: { total, limit, offset, hasMore } }
changes.note: `sort: 'updatedAt:desc'` becomes `orderBy: [{ updatedAt: 'desc' }]` (fields: createdAt, updatedAt, startsAt, expiresAt, status, recordType, ref, customId, sourceSystem, scopeType, scopeId, specificity, label). `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `startsAt` and `expiresAt` keep their names but are now a range object `{ gte, lte }`; the old string form is gone. `q`, `qFields` and `dataFilter` are unchanged (dataFilter is sent exactly as before). An option set to an empty string is now left out of the request.

changes.name: app.records.match
changes.note: `total` is `count`. `limit` was already in the input. With no `limit` it answers its usual 100 as before. With a `limit`, `nextCursor` is set when there are more: pass it back as `cursor` in the input.

changes.name: app.records.resolveAll
changes.note: `total` is `count`. `limit` was already in the input. With no `limit` it answers its usual 500 as before. With a `limit`, `nextCursor` is set when there are more: pass it back as `cursor`. The API cuts one answer at 1000, so a `limit` above 1000 (the old maximum was 5000) now needs the cursor to get the rest.

changes.name: app.threads.list
changes.before: { data, pagination: { total, limit, offset, hasMore } }
changes.note: `sort: 'lastReplyAt:desc'` becomes `orderBy: [{ lastReplyAt: 'desc' }]` (fields: createdAt, updatedAt, lastReplyAt, replyCount, status). `createdAt` and `updatedAt` keep their names but are now a range object `{ gte, lte }`; the old string form is gone. `parentIds` is sent exactly as before (comma-joined). An option set to an empty string is now left out of the request.

The standard words sit at the top of the body, beside limit and cursor: q (was query.search); orderBy: [{ updatedAt: 'desc' }] (was sort: [{ field, direction }]); createdAt / updatedAt: { gte, lte } (were query.createdAfter/Before, query.updatedAfter/Before); expand: ['facets'] (the route's expandFacets, never in the SDK type). The old names are refused by the API. orderBy fields: id, name, status, category, type, schemaType, sku, gtin, createdAt, updatedAt, sortOrder, groupKey. query.status / productIds / sku / gtin / facetEquals and includeDeleted are unchanged.

changes.name: initializeApi({ apiVersion })
changes.note: A version older than 2027-01 is ignored: SDK 3 always asks for at least its own version.

changes.name: paging by offset
changes.note: There is no offset or page number. Page forward with `cursor`; cache keys built on offset or page must use the cursor. For a numbered pager use the standard query.

changes.name: shared dependencies
changes.note: Built on SDK 3, a component declares shared-dependency contract v8 and gets SDK 3 from the host: as the import, as the `SL` prop and as the window global `SL3` (`SL` stays SDK 2). Keep building both formats: the host loads the UMD build of an app on SDK 3.

changes.name: unknown list options
changes.note: A list refuses a query option it does not read (400 UNKNOWN_PARAMETER) instead of ignoring it. Watch for one options object shared by an admin call and a public call (includeDeleted, contactId, assignedTo; status, includeScheduled and includeExpired on public app records).

changes.name: every list is one page
changes.note: A list returns 50 items unless you ask for another `limit`, and `nextCursor` says whether there are more. In SDK 2 many lists (products, variants, batches, proofs of a product, forms, templates, lots, claim sets, group members, an app's config items…) returned everything in one answer. Where the app needs them all, use `all((cursor) => x.list(…, { limit: 200, cursor }))` or follow `nextCursor`; where it shows a page, pass `limit` and `cursor`. The report marks each such call "used to return everything". The exception is a small fixed set (a page's widgets, facet definitions, config fields, a look-up by ids): always whole, no `limit` or `cursor`.

changes.name: one word for search, sort, dates and related data
changes.note: Search text is `q` (was `search`, `query`, `query.search`). Sorting is `orderBy: [{ field: 'asc' | 'desc' }]` (was `sort`, `order`, `sortBy` + `sortOrder`). A date field takes a range, `createdAt: { gte, lte }` (was `createdFrom`/`createdTo`, `recordedAfter`/`recordedBefore`, `query.createdAfter`/`Before`, or a `'gte:…'` string). Related things are `expand: ['items']` (was `includeItems`, `expandFacets`, `includes`, `include`). The time window of a log or schedule stays `from` / `to`. The API refuses the old spellings with the word to use, and refuses a sort field or related thing the list does not have. A bare sort field used to mean descending on app records, cases, threads and bookings: say the direction.
